title: The Fewest Moves to Make All the Numbers Equal

concept.title: The best meeting point of numbers on a line is the median
body: In one move you may **add 1 to a number or subtract 1 from it**. What is the smallest number of moves that makes all the numbers in a list **equal**? For `1 2 3` the answer is 2 (change both 1 and 3 to 2). For `1 10 2 9` it is 16.

If all the numbers become the value `x`, the moves needed are `|a[0] - x| + |a[1] - x| + ...`. Think of the numbers as people standing on a line who must all walk to the same house; the sum of the distances is smallest at the **median**. Reason: if `x` has more numbers on its left than on its right (or the same number), moving `x` one step to the right makes the sum smaller or equal when there are more numbers on the right, and the other way round. The point where the two sides are balanced is the median. So **sort the numbers, take the middle one, and add up the distances to it**.

body.code:
a.sort()
median = a[len(a) // 2]
print(sum(abs(x - median) for x in a))

body: For an even count any value between the two middle numbers gives the same sum, so either middle number works. The sum can reach 5 * 10^13, so 64-bit numbers are necessary. Another way to compute the same sum without the median: pair the smallest with the largest, the second smallest with the second largest, and add the distances of the pairs.

statement: A list of `n` integers is given. In one move you can increase or decrease one number by 1. Print the smallest number of moves after which all the numbers are equal.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of values.
outputFormat: Print the smallest number of moves.
hints: The sum of the distances to a point is smallest at the median.
Sort the numbers and take the middle one.
Add up the absolute differences; use 64-bit numbers.

explanation: The sum of the distances to a common value is smallest at the median, so the numbers are sorted, the middle one is taken and the absolute differences to it are added up.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(1) extra.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

a.sort()
median = a[n // 2]
print(sum(abs(x - median) for x in a))
